analysis: The closest option has a sustained developmental, social and psychological core. Lifespan development, psychopathology, health psychology, diagnostics and cognition are complemented by sociology, ethics, policy, rhetoric and actual primary-school teaching. These are direct developmental/support and complementary context/method contributions, not a claim to the UvA professional sequence.

The youth-support option retains developmental and social foundations while adding language acquisition and impairment, neurobiology, physiology, pharmacology, epidemiology, human rights and inclusive leadership. Removed infection/immunity, disease pathology, molecular-cell laboratory, advanced genetics and evolution that did not implement this concept strongly enough. Pharmacology and physiology have specific neural-treatment and health-foundation roles, bounded by the absence of professional child therapy.

The rights/family-policy option now has explicit developmental, social-psychological, youth-resilience and community-teaching anchors. Public economics, public policy, legal institutions, gender, racial exclusion and collective action support its social-environment emphasis. Rights courses are general rights reasoning rather than specialist child law. Removed environmental governance and excess generic politics/private-law weight. The selected social-movement course supplies a bounded analysis of collective responses to unequal conditions.

All three programmes have twenty-four unique courses and current offered terms, earlier formal prerequisites, Year-1 PPD and at least six advanced courses. Sociology foundations precede later theory; introductory statistics precedes advanced statistical methods; psychopathology precedes clinical assessment. Youth-support Psycholinguistics follows the brain gateway in its sole planned 2027h1 offering; its evidence does not impose additional entry requirements. Formal and useful advisory progression were inspected separately.

Thirteen positive correspondences recognise primary content or educational function without requiring equal credits or identical disciplinary scope. They cover development, peers/social processes, ethics, language/reading difficulties, educator support, practical child teaching, brain and behaviour, psychopathology, methods, qualitative inquiry, statistics, policy and diagnostics. Dedicated introductions, family pedagogy, personality, descriptive statistics, testing, professional skills, philosophy of science, single-case research, psychotherapeutic schools, thesis and open choice retain meaningful blanks. Optional UCR research is outside the 180 EC.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Academic writing, literature evaluation, civic collaboration and reflective practice provide the first-year common foundation.

BENECON111.name: Introduction to Economics
BENECON111.contribution: introduces economic reasoning about incentives, resources and government as a foundation for analysing public support and spending

BENECON311.name: Public Economics
BENECON311.contribution: analyses public goods, equity, taxation, education, health, welfare and social insurance using economic models and policy research

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: develops empirical research design, measurement, sampling, statistics and a complete ethically managed student data-collection project

BENLEAD211.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
BENLEAD211.contribution: studies emotion regulation, belonging and psychological safety in inclusive leadership, with a supervised original survey, measurement and empirical analysis; it complements the study of supportive social environments

GOSGATE102.name: Law, Society & Justice
GOSGATE102.contribution: introduces legal traditions, social justice and legal reasoning as foundations for investigating rights and public institutions affecting social life

GOSHIST112.name: Histories of Gender
GOSHIST112.contribution: examines gender, family, sexuality, health and exclusion through intersectional histories, oral inquiry and public storytelling; it supplies historical social context rather than child-development theory

GOSLAWJ111.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
GOSLAWJ111.contribution: examines legal and philosophical foundations of human rights, protection systems, dignity and competing moral claims; it supplies rights reasoning rather than a specialist children’s-rights course

GOSLAWJ213.name: Comparative Constitutional Law
GOSLAWJ213.contribution: compares constitutions, public institutions, judicial review, participation and administrative remedies as frameworks for analysing rights and public decision-making

GOSPHIL111.name: Introduction to Western Philosophy
GOSPHIL111.contribution: develops interpretation and criticism of philosophical arguments about knowledge, ethics, identity and mind

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics
GOSPHIL212.contribution: examines moral theories and ethical reasoning, enabling evaluation of values and competing interests in childrearing and education

GOSPHIL214.name: Philosophy of Mind
GOSPHIL214.contribution: examines mind, self, identity and consciousness through philosophical arguments and neuropsychological cases, complementing psychological accounts of development

GOSPOLI111.name: Introduction to Political Philosophy
GOSPOLI111.contribution: examines political ideas about authority, justice and collective life through primary texts, supporting normative analysis of social institutions

GOSPOLI112.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
GOSPOLI112.contribution: compares political institutions and democratic arrangements, providing foundations for policy and institutional analysis

GOSPOLI312.name: Public Policy Analysis
GOSPOLI312.contribution: examines policy-making phases and alternative conceptions of public policy through a sugar-policy case and policy memos; the contribution is policy analysis rather than specialised Dutch youth-care organisation

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.contribution: examines social identities, institutions, boundaries and inequality as the wider context of family, school and peer life

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: develops qualitative interviewing, documentary inquiry, interpretation and reflexivity for studying social experiences and institutions

GOSSOCI214.name: Modern Sociology
GOSSOCI214.contribution: examines modern social theory, power, inequality and cultural context through competing traditions and an empirical case paper

GOSSOCI215.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
GOSSOCI215.contribution: examines collective action and environmental justice through feminist, anticolonial and other perspectives, complementing the study of unequal social conditions and civic responses

GOSSOCI311.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
GOSSOCI311.contribution: examines trust, solidarity, civil society, public spheres and social repair through theory and research on an organisation or initiative

HCBBIOM111.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
HCBBIOM111.contribution: examines population health, inequality, epidemiological designs, confounding and intervention evaluation as methods for studying developmental risk and prevention

HCBBIOM311.name: Pharmacology
HCBBIOM311.contribution: examines drug action, including neural and psychoactive treatment mechanisms and an experimental proposal; it supplies bounded biological treatment foundations rather than professional child therapy

HCBCOGN112.name: Neurobiology
HCBCOGN112.contribution: develops neural and cellular explanations of nervous-system function as biological foundations for cognition and developmental differences

HCBCOGN212.name: Perception & Action
HCBCOGN212.contribution: examines neural mechanisms of perception and action, complementing the cognitive and biological study of development

HCBCOGN311.name: Higher Order Functions
HCBCOGN311.contribution: examines attention, memory, emotion, control and social cognition, including an attentional-blink experiment and research proposal

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.contribution: examines language acquisition and processing, reading, dyslexia and language impairments using psycholinguistic evidence and experimental methods

HCBGATE101.name: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
HCBGATE101.contribution: introduces cellular, molecular and genetic foundations needed for the selected physiology and pharmacology sequence; it supports the biological strand rather than serving as child pedagogy

HCBGATE102.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
HCBGATE102.contribution: introduces brain and behaviour relationships as a foundation for developmental, cognitive and psychological inquiry

HCBLIFE212.name: Human Physiology
HCBLIFE212.contribution: examines organ systems, homeostasis and stress responses as biological context for health, behaviour and supportive interventions

HCBPSYC111.name: Social Psychology
HCBPSYC111.contribution: studies social influence, identity, group processes, prejudice, prosocial behaviour and close relationships through empirical psychological research

HCBPSYC211.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
HCBPSYC211.contribution: develops experimental design, statistical modelling, assumption checks and interpretation in health and behavioural research

HCBPSYC212.name: Psychopathology
HCBPSYC212.contribution: examines psychopathology across the lifespan, classification, biopsychosocial explanations and treatment, using cases and critical literature synthesis

HCBPSYC311.name: Medical & Health Psychology
HCBPSYC311.contribution: examines health, illness, prevention, stress and healthcare relationships, with culturally attentive interviewing and clinical-health case formulation

HCBPSYC312.name: Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies
HCBPSYC312.contribution: introduces diagnostic reasoning, tests and interviews, ethics and major psychotherapies, with introductory assessment practice and an integrated case report

HCBPSYC313.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
HCBPSYC313.contribution: develops systematic review and meta-analysis, bias appraisal, effect-size calculation and evidence synthesis for behavioural and health questions

HCBPSYC314.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
HCBPSYC314.contribution: examines physical, cognitive, emotional, social and personality development from prenatal life onward, including attachment, education, culture and developmental psychopathology

HCBPSYC315.name: Youth Resilience to Extremism
HCBPSYC315.contribution: studies adolescent risk, belonging and prevention of extremism and produces research-based teacher-training materials and a youth toolkit for an inclusive school project

MCCCOMM111.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
MCCCOMM111.contribution: develops rhetorical argument, audience awareness and public communication as complementary skills for explaining social and developmental questions

MCCCOMM213.name: Rhetoric in Action
MCCCOMM213.contribution: develops age-appropriate public-speaking and storytelling activities with local primary-school children, on-site coaching and reflection on community-engaged teaching

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.contribution: examines persuasion, framing and ethical communication through community projects, supporting responsible public explanation and youth-support communication

MCCMEDI311.name: Media & Race
MCCMEDI311.contribution: examines racial construction, exclusion, youth and marginalised storytelling through media, archives and participatory inquiry, complementing critical study of children’s social environments

alignment.rationale: Both examine language and reading development and difficulties. UvA also addresses mathematics, school support and educational interventions; UCR focuses on language processing and experimental psycholinguistics.
Both connect nervous-system function and behaviour. UvA situates this study in the pedagogical curriculum; UCR provides a broad introductory brain-and-behaviour foundation.

Both study social relationships, group influences and behaviour as contexts of development. UvA specifically examines children’s peers and leisure, including developmental risks and protection; UCR studies social processes more broadly.
Both develop inferential statistical reasoning and analysis for behavioural or social research. UCR includes experimental design and multivariable modelling.
Both examine psychological difficulties, their explanations, risk and treatment. UvA focuses on developmental psychopathology in childhood and adolescence; UCR covers disorders across the lifespan.

Both develop diagnostic reasoning, selection and interpretation of tests and interviews, ethical awareness and case-based assessment. UvA focuses on child and pedagogical contexts; UCR combines broader introductory psychodiagnostics with psychotherapy.
Both study physical, cognitive, emotional and social development, its theories and environmental influences. UCR continues across adulthood, while UvA concentrates on conception through adolescence.

Both examine how educators and educational environments support children’s development. UCR creates teacher resources for resilience and inclusion; UvA compares educator roles, relationships and quality across childcare, school and youth care.
Both examine qualitative research questions and methods, interpretation and research quality. UCR develops broader qualitative social inquiry.
Both examine policy theories, processes, actors and analysis. UvA applies them to education and youth care; UCR uses a different policy case and policy-memo practice.
Both develop research design, measurement, sampling, validity and an empirical research cycle. UCR uses a broader student project rather than a specifically pedagogical focus.

Both critically examine ethical theories, values and competing interests. UvA applies philosophical argument specifically to education, childrearing, rights and paternalism; UCR supplies broader moral theory.

Both provide child-focused practical experience and reflection. UCR works with primary-school partners on rhetorical teaching and coaching; UvA requires an approved internship with broader pedagogical practice or research and formal supervision.
No selected course provides the combined introductory survey of pedagogical and educational sciences and their professional fields.
No selected course provides the dedicated second introductory survey of pedagogical and educational fields and practice.
UCR Research Methods & Statistics contains descriptive statistics but is placed with Research Methodology as its strongest overall relationship. It is not counted a second time here.
Rhetoric and inclusive communication complement professional interaction but do not directly reproduce the structured basic counselling, listening and reflective interview training.

Selected assessment and research courses cover measurement, reliability and validity, but their strongest overall placements are Diagnostics and Research Methodology; no separate testing module is counted here.
Sociology and developmental psychology provide context, but no selected course centres family pedagogy, transactional parent-child interactions, parenting support and maltreatment.
Personality development is part of Lifespan Developmental Psychology, placed with Developmental Psychology. No separate selected course centres personality theory.
No selected course directly reproduces the advanced child and adolescent interviewing and creative professional conversation sequence.
General philosophy and research methods provide foundations, but no selected course centres philosophy of scientific explanation and disciplinary knowledge.
Selected research courses develop empirical projects and evidence synthesis; none centres the external module’s single-case experimental designs and individual change analysis.
The scheduled UCR courses do not include a required individual pedagogical empirical thesis. Optional independent research is shown separately outside the scheduled credits.
Introductory UCR assessment is placed with Diagnostics. No additional selected module reproduces the advanced child-focused professional assessment and advice sequence.
Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies includes major therapeutic approaches, but its strongest overall placement is Diagnostics. It is not counted a second time here.
Open space remains unspecified; no elective or minor is invented as a comparator course.
